title: Doomed Love
author: Camilo Castelo Branco
place: Portuguese Centre of Photography, former Cadeia da Relação prison
description: Amor de Perdição: Camilo Castelo Branco wrote this tragic romance in 1862, soon after his release from Porto’s Relação jail, where he had been held for adultery. The jail is now the Portuguese Centre of Photography.

title: Log Book: Selected Poems
author: Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen
description: Poems by Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen, one of Portugal’s best-loved poets, translated by Richard Zenith. She was born in Porto in 1919 and grew up in the house and gardens that are now the city’s Botanical Garden.

title: Forbidden Words: Selected Poetry
author: Eugénio de Andrade
place: Eugénio de Andrade Poetry Library, Foz
description: Short, sensual poems by Eugénio de Andrade, translated by Alexis Levitin. Andrade lived in Porto for more than 50 years, and his last home, facing the mouth of the Douro at Foz, is now a library of poetry.

title: Prince Henry ‘the Navigator’: A Life
author: Peter Russell
description: Oxford historian Peter Russell’s biography of Prince Henry, which separates the man from the legend of a scholar-prince sending ships into the unknown. Henry is said to have been born in this riverside house in 1394.

title: Port and the Douro
author: Richard Mayson
place: Port wine lodges, Cais de Gaia
description: Wine writer Richard Mayson’s standard history of port, from the terraced vineyards of the Douro valley to the shippers’ lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the river from Porto, where the wine has been aged and blended for centuries.

title: The Factory House at Oporto
author: John Delaforce
place: Factory House, Rua do Infante Dom Henrique
description: A history of the Factory House by John Delaforce, from a family of port shippers. The granite club, finished around 1790, has been the meeting place of Porto’s British port merchants ever since.

title: Journey to Portugal
author: José Saramago
description: Viagem a Portugal: José Saramago, later a Nobel laureate, drove the length of his country in 1979 and wrote about it in the third person. His long Porto chapter climbs from the river to the cathedral and the steep old streets around it.
